CARD_1.TEXT_1: At Montaraz Outdoors & Culture, we organize active and cultural holidays. Our trips bring you closer to nature, local culture, and the people, always with personal guidance and a deep love for the land. Whether you choose a relaxing bike tour, a challenging mountain hike, or an adventurous family trip, we create unforgettable experiences, fully tailored to your wishes.

CARD_2.TEXT_1: Time outdoors, time together. Our family holidays combine adventure, local culture and the joy of discovering new places together — with the kind of moments families remember long after the trip.

CARD_3.TITLE: Cycling Holidays
CARD_3.TEXT_1: Discover places at the perfect pace. Our cycling holidays combine scenic routes, local culture and the freedom to explore in your own way. Whether by e-bike, mountain bike or on a relaxed recreational ride, each trip is designed to enjoy the outdoors, connect with the surroundings and create memorable experiences.

CARD_4.TEXT_1: Discover Spain step by step, through landscapes that change from mountain peaks to quiet villages and open countryside. Whether it’s an easy walk or a more demanding trek, every journey is tailored to your level and pace, with the freedom to truly experience the outdoors.
CARD_4.WHAT_DO_WE_EXPECT_1: - Day hikes with easy to moderate intensity, combining nature and culture
CARD_4.WHAT_DO_WE_EXPECT_2: - Multi-day treks, with or without luggage transport
CARD_4.WHAT_DO_WE_EXPECT_3: - Nature and culture routes: hiking through mountains, gorges, villages, and olive groves
CARD_4.WHAT_DO_WE_EXPECT_4: - Local stops: time to enjoy a drink, taste tapas, or explore a charming village

TREKKING_ALPUJARRAS.WHAT_TO_BRING_TEXT_1: Weather is important to consider while packing for your outdoor activity. Your packing list is based on your comfort and sensitivity. Layering your clothes is the best way to travel and be outdoors. It is highly recommended as the best way to stay warm and cool, as the weather is bound to change in the mountains.

TREKKING_ALPUJARRAS.DIFFICULTY_3: Proper hiking equipment is required. Walking sticks are recommended, and ankle-high hiking boots are strongly recommended.
TREKKING_ALPUJARRAS.DIFFICULTY_4: If you're unsure whether this trail is right for you or your group, feel free to contact us — we're happy to help you choose the best option!
TREKKING_ALPUJARRAS.WHAT_TO_EXPECT_TEXT_1: Hiking in the rich Andalusian culture and history with the natural beauty of picturesque landscapes, charming villages, and iconic landmarks.
TREKKING_ALPUJARRAS.WHAT_TO_EXPECT_TEXT_2: Your main luggage is taken between the villages along the route. This leaves you free to hike with a light bag with the essentials you need during the day. Hiking with a light backpack is much more pleasant than dragging a heavy rucksack, allowing you to enjoy the landscape without a heavy load. The trekking takes you through the picturesque Alpujarra region on the southern slopes of the Sierra Nevada, Spain's highest mountain range. It seems like a journey back in time, as the area has its unique culture from ancient times to the present day, shown in its food culture, architecture, and traditions. The main feature of the outstanding landscape is the villages situated mainly above 1.000 m. They are made up of white, square-shaped houses with flat roofs spreading out across the valleys. The adventure sets out from the village of Laroles located near the pass of La Ragua, the only connection between the north and south of the Sierra Nevada, and heading toward the west.
TREKKING_ALPUJARRAS.WHAT_TO_EXPECT_TEXT_3: During the journey, you will discover the many villages and their terraced fields climbing the slopes presenting beautiful views and dramatic landscapes of the mountain range. The blossoms of spring and the colors of autumn are the ideal time to join the trekking making it a unique experience.
TREKKING_ALPUJARRAS.WHAT_TO_EXPECT_TEXT_4: Join us and uncover the hidden beauty of the Alpujarra region a treasure to discover!

DAY_1.TEXT_1: Upon arrival in Málaga or Granada, our pick-up will drive us to our rural hotel in the Guadix region located between the north of the Sierra Nevada Mountain Range and the Gorafe desert, one of the unique landscapes of the province of Granada. Upon arrival in Málaga or Granada, our pick-up will drive us to our rural hotel in the Guadix region located between the north of the Sierra Nevada Mountain Range and the Gorafe desert, one of the unique landscapes of the province of Granada. The tour leader will organize dinner to celebrate the first day of the journey.

DAY_2.SUBTITLE: Trail 1 Laroles – Válor
DAY_2.TEXT_1: After breakfast, we drive over the mountain pass “Puerto La Ragua” to the trekking starting point in the Laroles village. The trail starts at the upper part of the village, at 1000 meters above sea level, from where you can see the flat roofs of the town's houses. One of the defining elements of the territory that reaches its maximum significance in the Alpujarra region is the architecture with values from other cultures and civilizations. The orography and relief of the terrain influence the profile of the towns. These villages are distributed and oriented towards the south so that the sun offers them its luminosity and keeps them warm for as long as possible in the cold winters. Most of these towns are located in the middle of the slopes that descend from the top of the Sierra Nevada in a stepped composition that gives them a charm.
DAY_2.TEXT_2: Dinner: The tour leader will organize a dinner.

DAY_3.SUBTITLE: Trail 2 Válor – Mecina Bombarón
DAY_3.TEXT_1: We leave the village of Válor which was the homeland of the Alpujarra hero Aben Humeya, a descendant of the Umayyad caliphs, who was proclaimed King of the Alpujarra after the Moorish uprising against the Christians in the reign of Philip II, back in 1568. The second hike will take us to Yegen, a peaceful village where the romantic traveler Gerald Brenan lived known as the author of “Al Sur de Granada”, one of the best-known books about the Alpujarra. After crossing the Mecina River and a steep climb we reach the village of Mecina Bombarón. After we take the car that brings us to our next hotel nearby in the village of Cádiar located between the Sierra Nevada and the Contraviesa mountain range.
DAY_3.TEXT_2: Dinner: The tour leader will organize a dinner.

DAY_4.SUBTITLE: Trail 3 Cádiar - Trevélez
DAY_4.TEXT_1: Today's stage will be more demanding. It will take us from the southernmost point of the Alpujarra trail (800 meters) to the highest trekking point, about 1.500 meters above sea level, in the village of Trevélez. Besides being the highest village in the Sierra Nevada, Trevélez is renowned for its naturally cured hams, benefiting from the healthy air of Sierra Nevada. In the 19th century, the ham of Trevélez gained recognition when Queen Isabel II granted it the distinction of being a supplier to the Royal House. It currently holds the Denomination of Origin and has attained worldwide recognition.
DAY_4.TEXT_2: Shortened Route Available: There is also the option to shorten the trail, making it more accessible for those who want a lighter version of the hike to meet the same level as the other days.
DAY_4.TEXT_3: Dinner: The tour leader will organize a dinner.

DAY_5.SUBTITLE: Trail 4 Trevélez – La Taha
DAY_5.TEXT_1: Today, the trail takes you through a forest of holm oaks which in autumn offers a colorful and impressive valley. In spring the gorse and broom come into bloom, producing a sea of bright yellow flowers. The panoramic views we pass expose the rugged landscapes with deep valleys and large slopes of the Alpujarra region. Isolated places like ravines are home to many species of fauna and flora due to microclimates characterized by freezing temperatures in winter and mild temperatures in summer. After crossing two ravines and a long descent the path arrives at the village of Busquístar near our destination for today called “La Taha”, a municipality that consists of several beautiful small towns. The name derives from the administrative divisions of the ancient Kingdom of Granada during the Nasrid era. It is a peaceful place with stunning views, preserving well-maintained traditional neighborhoods in the Alpujarra.
DAY_5.TEXT_2: Dinner: The tour leader will organize a dinner.

DAY_6.SUBTITLE: Trail 5 La Taha – Capileira
DAY_6.TEXT_1: Today's last stage is an upward trail with a long ascent in the morning that brings us to our last destination, the village of Capileira, the highest of the three small towns located at 1.435 meters in the gorge of the Poqueira River. The Poqueira Gorge and the three villages on its slopes have become one of the most iconic sights of the Alpujarra Mountains. It is located at the foot of the highest peaks and contains one of the most surprising landscapes of the Sierra Nevada Natural Park. Here we stay for the last two nights of the trekking.

DAY_7.SUBTITLE: Free day Capileira
DAY_7.TEXT_1: Explore the Historic-Artistic site of Poqueira River Valley and the three villages; Pampaneira, Bubión, and Capileira.
DAY_7.TEXT_2: Although its origins date back to the Phoenicians, Romans, and Visigoths, the strongest legacy is left by the Arabs. The traditional architecture with typical white houses and flat roofs built along steep and winding streets, irrigation systems, agriculture, and linguistic roots are the inheritance left by a culture that was present for eight hundred years.
DAY_7.TEXT_3: For the enthusiasts, there is the option to join the guide for an extra hike in the area.
DAY_7.TEXT_4: The guide will organize a place to have dinner together to celebrate the last evening of the journey.

DAY_1.TEXT_1: One of the most beautiful routes in Sierra Nevada National Park is the Old Mine Trail. This historic path, built at the end of the 19th century to access the mines, follows the Genil River toward the confluence of several rivers at the very end of the valley. The valley reveals its stunning scenery, including the rugged north faces of the highest peaks in the Sierra Nevada: Mulhacén, Veleta, and Alcazaba. Throughout the day you come across ruins of stone buildings, old mine tunnels, and the typical Iberian Ibex or the golden eagles are common to see. To get to the starting point of the trail we drive approx. 30 min. to the beautiful village of Güéjar Sierra, a mountain town located at 1.000 meters on the northwestern slope of the Sierra Nevada National Park.

DAY_1.TEXT_1: We drive to the village Monachil, located in a fertile valley of the Sierra Nevada Mountain Range at 800 meters above sea level, just outside Granada. The walking path, called Cahorros Trail, is a hiking path in the lower hills of Sierra Nevada National Park. The trail starts in the village following the river up toward the entrance of the narrow gorge. The way becomes a succession of stairs, crawling under overhanging rocks, and crossing hanging bridges along a cascading river through the canyon that creates rockpools and caves, making the walk an adventure for the whole family. At the end of the gorge, we return by a higher route, from which you get stunning views of the lush Monachil Valley. A great escape from the city and a perfect family day out in the mountains!

DAY_1.TITLE: Day 1
DAY_1.TEXT_1: The route starts at Europe’s southernmost ski resort and follows a great ascent along the San Juan Valley towards the second-highest peak of the mountain range, Veleta 3.392 meters. The trail brings you to the Carihuela Refuge located in the mountain pass “Collado de la Veleta” on its southern slope at an altitude of 3.200 meters where you can see the remains of the trenches from the Civil War.
DAY_1.TEXT_2: Before our eyes, a wide landscape of the Mediterranean mountain range opens, and the peak Mulhacén rises majestically. The trails continue to the “Caldera Lagoon” of glacial origin and one of the most emblematic lagoons in the Sierra Nevada. From the mountain refuge, the iconic steep climb awaits us up to the peak of Mulhacén. We take the same path to return to the mountain village.
DAY_1.TEXT_3: We classify the north-face route as a moderate + trail and has characteristics of altitude hiking. The hike involves a significant height difference with a long ascent and descent divided into two parts during the entire hike. A steep summit climb on rocky and loose terrain. The descent is less strenuous but can be tough on the knees. The trail doesn’t have any technical obstacles. For more information check our blog and look for “Trail grades”
DAY_1.TEXT_4: Optional: there is a minibus or the summer ski lift at your disposal, which leaves us at around 3.000 meters, a significant reduction of ascent, distance, and the demands of the route. Ask for more information.

DAY_2.TEXT_2: From the refuge, we hike gradually up toward Caldera Lagoon following the Mulhacén River through alpine meadows and rocky terrain, with panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys.
DAY_2.TEXT_3: One of the most emblematic lagoons in the Sierra Nevada, Caldera Lagoon, sits below the ridges of Mulhacén. After having a rest at the mountain refuge, the iconic steep climb awaits us up to the peak of Mulhacén. Once at the summit, you’ll be rewarded with breathtaking views of the surrounding peaks and valleys.
DAY_2.TEXT_4: After enjoying your time at the summit, we begin the descent back along the south slope of Mulhacén to 2.700 meters altitude where we take the shuttle bus back to the village of Capileira in the Alpujarra region.
DAY_2.TEXT_5: After relaxing with a drink and a tapa in the white village we drive back to Granada.
DAY_2.TEXT_6: We classify the route as a challenging trail with characteristics of altitude hiking. The land that charmed romantic travelers still captivates anybody who visits it. The Cycling Journey takes you along epic, ever-changing landscapes from a vast high plateau to desert landscapes, high mountains with traditional villages, and the tropical Mediterranean coast towards Granada.

DAY_1.TEXT_1: Upon arrival either in Málaga or Granada, our pick-up will drive us to our hotel in Granada.
DAY_1.TEXT_2: A city with history located at the foot of the Sierra Nevada mountains. The cultural riches of Granada with influences from the Moors, Catholics, and Jews make this city in Spain into an important cultural center with Moorish rule spanning 800 years of occupation.
DAY_1.TEXT_3: In the afternoon there is the optional guided tour of Alhambra and the gardens of the Generalife for those who have pre-reserved the activity.
DAY_1.TEXT_4: The rest of the day you are free to explore more beautiful places and to try the Granada tapas which are known for serving free tapas with every drink.
DAY_1.TEXT_5: The tour guide will organize a place to have dinner together to celebrate the first evening of the journey.

DAY_2.STRONG_1: Track 1 In search of cave dwellings
DAY_2.TEXT_1: After breakfast, our pick-up will drive us to the starting point of the first cycle ride in search of the cave dwellings located northeast of Granada. The tour leader will give an introductory briefing about the trip, followed by a safety and bicycle technical briefing. After the briefing, you can try out your bicycles and make minor adjustments to ensure comfort.
DAY_2.TEXT_2: We start to pedal through the mountainous landscape, a route of tranquility and beauty of great historical-cultural and natural interest belonging to the territory of the Granada Geopark, which was declared a UNESCO Global Geopark.
DAY_2.TEXT_3: After passing several villages, the road leads us to the old town of Guadix, showing an important heritage of monuments, with the medieval Arab Citadel, the Cathedral, and various Mudejar-style buildings. The most characteristic feature is that many of the inhabitants of this large town live in cave houses.
DAY_2.TEXT_4: After a visit to the cave houses, we will cycle to our cave hotel, where we will stay the second night.

DAY_3.TEXT_1: A route through a beautiful region of white mountain villages nestled between the southern slopes of the Sierra Nevada and the Mediterranean Sea.
DAY_3.TEXT_2: The Alpujarra is an area where time seems to stand still. It is the last redoubt of the Moriscos from Granada showing the symbiosis between man and the environment reached by the Moorish culture of Al-Andalus.
DAY_3.TEXT_3: We start the day by driving to “Puerto de la Ragua”, a mountain pass at an elevation of 2.000 meters, located on the boundary of Granada and Almería provinces. The route passes through picturesque villages with stunning views over the valley and its terraced farms. On clear days, it’s possible to see the Mediterranean Sea and even Africa.
DAY_3.TEXT_4: Along the way, there is time to stop and explore some of the rustic villages having a very distinct architecture as a result of the Berber occupation: flat-roofed, box-shaped white houses with tall round chimneys, clustered along narrow, winding, and steep streets, clinging to the mountains of the Sierra Nevada.
DAY_3.TEXT_5: Our next hotel is a “cortijada”, a traditional group of homesteads and farm buildings, that has been transformed into a hotel.

DAY_4.TEXT_1: After breakfast, we drive back to the higher part of the Alpujarras to continue the journey with our first destination the village Trevélez, one of the highest villages in Spain located at 1.480 meters in the Trevélez Gorge. It is well known for ham drying in a traditional way, which has its own Denomination of Origin for its quality and great flavor.
DAY_4.TEXT_2: There is an optional ham tour for those who have pre-reserved the activity.
DAY_4.TEXT_3: Then we keep cycling towards the village Capileira, at 1.435 meters, the highest of the three villages in the Poquiera Gorge, one of the most beautiful places in the Alpujarras. A truly great experience to stay the night with the breathtaking landscapes of the southern slopes of Sierra Nevada.

DAY_5.STRONG_1: Track 4 The Route of the Old Oil Train
DAY_5.TEXT_1: A ride through the beautiful Lecrín Valley, a mixture of pine forest and cultivated land, towards the Tropical Coast of Granada.
DAY_5.TEXT_2: We leave the Alpujarras behind us and drive to the highest village of the Lecrín Valley where we stay the last night of the tour.
DAY_5.TEXT_3: There is an optional Olive oil tour in the morning for those who have pre-reserved the activity.
DAY_5.TEXT_4: Our last cycle day takes us through the Lecrín Valley, an area of rolling hills, ravines, rugged cliffs, and rivers covered with cultivated citrus and orange groves, almond trees, and olive oil plantations.
DAY_5.TEXT_5: We go towards the viewpoint where the Mediterranean Sea comes into view with our destination the village of Salobreña.
DAY_5.TEXT_6: Next, after enjoying a swim and a drink, we will head back to our rural hotel where we will celebrate our last evening of the cycle journey.

DAY_6.TEXT_1: The journey ends after breakfast. There will be a private airport transfer from the hotel to the airport in Granada or Málaga.

WHAT_TO_EXPECT.TITLE: What to expect
WHAT_TO_EXPECT.TEXT_1: A cycling journey from Ronda to Córdoba is an unforgettable exploration through the heart of Andalusia. You’ll ride through a landscape full of contrasts: rugged mountains, quiet olive groves, charming white villages, and impressive historic cities. This trip is ideal for those who want to combine tranquility, culture, and nature, without rushing.
WHAT_TO_EXPECT.TEXT_2: You cycle on quiet country roads with little traffic. The route is hilly, with a few challenging climbs and a flat stage on the last day, suitable for recreational cyclists on an E-bike with a good basic fitness level. (See E-bike difficulty level in BLOG) Along the way, mountain panoramas, olive fields, and authentic villages alternate.
WHAT_TO_EXPECT.TEXT_3: Each evening you arrive at a carefully selected hotel, usually small-scale and peacefully located.
WHAT_TO_EXPECT.TEXT_7: Average 40–80 km cycling per day (4–6 hours including breaks)
WHAT_TO_EXPECT.TEXT_8: Time for a terrace, lunch, photos, and sightseeing along the way
WHAT_TO_EXPECT.TEXT_9: Arrival in the afternoon, time to relax or explore the surroundings
WHAT_TO_EXPECT.TEXT_10: Finish your journey in the impressive city of Córdoba, with its famous Mezquita and atmospheric old town

DAY_1.TEXT_1: Upon arrival in Málaga, our transfer will take us to our rural hotel in Ronda, located above a deep gorge that divides the city in two. The tour leader will organize an introductory meeting about the trip, followed by a safety briefing.
DAY_1.TEXT_2: Start the day by exploring Ronda’s famous sights, such as the iconic bridge or the Plaza de Toros, Spain’s oldest bullring. Or take a trip to one of the many local vineyards, an excellent way to deepen your knowledge of local wines.
DAY_1.TEXT_3: The tour leader will organize dinner to celebrate the first day of the journey.
DAY_1.TEXT_4: The hotel features a quietly located swimming pool

DAY_2.STRONG_1: Track 1 Sierra de las Nieves Mountain Range
DAY_2.TEXT_1: Off we go to the breathtaking Gaitanes Gorge, one of the most spectacular landscapes in the Malaga mountains where we stay the second night of the trip.
DAY_2.TEXT_2: We leave our hotel along meandering country roads, passing through the Ronda Mountain Range and the Sierra de las Nieves National Park, a 100% stunning landscape. After a picnic lunch at a panoramic viewpoint, we continue toward our hotel nestled in the heart of the Natural Park.
DAY_2.TEXT_5: The hotel features a quietly located swimming pool

DAY_3.TEXT_1: After breakfast, we drive the first kilometers with our support vehicle to skip the steep part and bring us higher where we start our second stage.
DAY_3.TEXT_2: Today we cycle through rural Andalusia, a mountainous and colorful landscape where Mediterranean crops alternate with pastureland. After the picnic lunch, we continue to the village of Antequera with its rich historical center that claims to have the most churches per inhabitant in Spain. Monasteries, palaces, the Moorish fortress, and prehistoric dolmens are some of the many sights.
DAY_3.TEXT_3: Hotel features a quietly located swimming pool

DAY_4.TEXT_1: Today is the only time we drive to our new starting point, a village built on the ruins of an old Moorish castle that overlooks the beautiful valley and lake below.
DAY_4.TEXT_2: The route takes us through the olive groves of Andalusia in the Sierras Subbéticas Natural Park and Geopark. Spain has olive groves spread throughout almost the entire country, but the largest concentration is in Andalusia, with locations where olive trees were already used when the region Hispania Baetica supplied olive oil to the Roman capital.
DAY_4.TEXT_3: Our destination today is the village of Priego de Córdoba in the heart of the natural park. For dinner, we offer you the opportunity to learn how to taste and appreciate olive oil with all your senses through an olive oil master, discovering the smell, aroma, and taste of each olive oil.
DAY_4.TEXT_4: Discover the old part of the village

DAY_5.STRONG_1: Stage 4 The Route of the Old Olive Oil Train
DAY_5.TEXT_1: Today we continue cycling through the beautiful landscapes of the Sierras Subbéticas that take us to picturesque villages.
DAY_5.TEXT_2: After another outdoor picnic, we follow the track of the old train route called “Vía Verde” that runs between olive trees and vineyards. These Greenways in Spain have been restored for cyclists and walkers.
DAY_5.TEXT_3: The route of the old oil train brings us to our next accommodation, a traditional Andalusian farmhouse converted into a hotel.

DAY_6.STRONG_1: Stage 5 The Caliphate and Mozarabic Route
DAY_6.TEXT_1: On your last cycling day, we follow two historic routes that lead us to the city of Córdoba, our final destination. The Caliphate Route is the Andalusian heritage that connects Córdoba and Granada, the capitals of the Caliphate and Nasrid al-Andalus. It was one of the busiest paths of the Iberian Peninsula in the Middle Ages, used by merchants from all over the known world, who supplied and traded with these important population centers; it was also the route of knowledge, science, and art.
DAY_6.TEXT_2: The other historic route is the Mozarabic Way to Santiago de Compostela. An ancient path that pays tribute to all Christians, the Mozarabs, who remained in the areas of Al-Andalus. A journey that reminds us of that time when these Christians, despite oppression, maintained their faith and devotion.
DAY_6.TEXT_3: The last part of the longest cycling route reveals our travel destination with views of the city of Córdoba, located in the Guadalquivir depression formed by the Guadalquivir River.

DAY_7.TEXT_1: Explore the city’s history and culture known for its unique blend of Roman, Moorish, and Christian influences. The city was once a significant Roman settlement and later became the capital of the Islamic Emirate and then the Caliphate of Córdoba, under which it flourished as one of the largest and most advanced cities in the world during the Middle Ages.
DAY_7.TEXT_2: In the morning there is an optional tour of the Mosque of Córdoba for those who have pre-reserved the activity.
DAY_7.TEXT_3: The tour guide will organize a place to have dinner together to celebrate the last evening of the journey

DAY_8.TEXT_1: The journey ends after breakfast at our hotel. There will be a private airport transfer from the hotel to the airport in Málaga.

DAY_1.TEXT_1: A cultural tour of the Alpujarras offers a captivating journey through stunning landscapes and rich traditions. Starting from the city of Granada, we embark on a scenic drive toward the village Trevélez located in the heart of the Natural Park Sierra Nevada. The town is considered one of the highest in Spain and is renowned for its high-quality ham. We will visit a traditional ham drying room “Secadero”, where you will learn about curing ham and finish with an Iberian ham tasting.
DAY_1.TEXT_2: Afterward, we continue our journey through the picturesque Alpujarras, heading towards the village Pórtugos to see the beautiful orange waterfall called “Fuente Agria” which means Fountain of Sourness. Traditionally, this water is used by the people in the Alpujarras for medicinal purposes due to the high concentration of minerals in the water.
DAY_1.TEXT_3: Next, we go to the enchanting three white villages “Pampaneira, Bubión, and Capileira”. The villages, with their distinctive whitewashed buildings and narrow, winding streets, offer a glimpse into the region’s Moorish heritage. Here, we enjoy a great lunch, savoring local cuisine in Capileira, the highest town of the three.
DAY_1.TEXT_4: Later on, we stop in Pampaneira to have a little walk, buy local products, and enjoy the serene beauty of the surrounding mountains.
DAY_1.TEXT_5: Before we head back to Granada, we stop one more time at “Puente de Tablate”, the bridge and Gateway to the Alpujarras. Over the centuries this site has been the key location in many battles.
DAY_1.TEXT_6: This tour provides a perfect blend of cultural immersion and natural beauty, making it an unforgettable experience.
